body.heading: Small tears, real damage
paragraphs: A sharp reply. A forgotten promise. A joke that landed wrong. None of these end relationships on their own, but unrepaired, they pile up into a distance that nobody can quite explain.
The good news: small ruptures need small repairs. What they cannot survive is being ignored and hoped away.

body.heading: The shape of a good repair
paragraphs: Name it plainly and soon: 'I've been thinking about what I said yesterday. It came out sharper than I meant.' No defending, no 'but you' — those come later, if at all.
Then listen to the effect, not just your intention. 'I didn't mean it that way' may be true, but 'I can see it landed badly' is what actually mends things.

description: Relationships rarely break from one big thing — they fray from small tears nobody mended.
